comparison: Unrestricted eating window with exercise-matched control
intervention: Time-restricted eating (TRE) with 4-12 hour feeding window combined with exercise
outcome: Body composition measures including fat mass (FM) in kg, body fat percentage (BF%), and fat-free mass (FFM) in kg
population: Adults performing exercise (including aerobic, resistance, or concurrent training)
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether time-restricted eating (TRE) combined with various forms of exercise (aerobic, resistance, or concurrent training) improves body composition outcomes, specifically reducing fat mass and body fat percentage while preserving fat-free mass, in adults compared to unrestricted eating with exercise.

comparison: Obese patients without type 2 diabetes mellitus receiving the same formula diet intervention
intervention: Very low calorie diets (<800 kcal/day) or low-energy liquid-formula diets (>800 kcal/day) using total diet replacement
outcome: Weight loss (final weight loss in kg, rate of weight loss in kg per week)
population: Obese patients (BMI 35.5-42.6 kg/m²) with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis compares weight losses following very low calorie diets (<800 kcal/day) or low-energy liquid-formula diets (>800 kcal/day) in obese patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus versus obese patients without type 2 diabetes mellitus.

comparison: Patients without OSA or with varying OSA severity levels; pre-bariatric metabolic surgery status
exposure: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and OSA-related indicators including apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) and intermittent hypoxia
outcome: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) presence, severity, and resolution assessed through multiple liver outcome tests including liver biopsy, NAFLD activity score (NAS), steatosis, fibrosis, inflammation, and serum markers (ALT, AST)
population: Adults with obesity (BMI ≥ 35)
research_question: This systematic review examines which obstructive sleep apnea (OSA)-related indicators can predict the presence of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) in patients with obesity, and assesses the effect of bariatric metabolic surgery (BMS) on improving both OSA and NAFLD over time.

comparison: Factors facilitating engagement versus factors hindering engagement (barriers versus facilitators)
intervention: Synchronous (real-time), remote health interventions for weight management
outcome: Engagement with remote weight management interventions (barriers and facilitators to engagement mapped to capability, opportunity, and motivation domains)
population: Adults aged 18 years or older with BMI ≥27.5 kg/m² (living with excess weight or obesity)
research_question: This systematic review examines the barriers and facilitators influencing engagement of adults living with excess weight (BMI ≥27.5 kg/m²) in synchronous, remote health interventions for weight management, with findings mapped to the COM-B model of behaviour change and Theoretical Domains Framework.

comparison: Children with different-sex (heterosexual) parents
exposure: Having gender and sexual minority (LGBTQ) parents
outcome: Mental health outcomes and mental health problems in children
population: Children with gender and sexual minority (LGBTQ) parents
research_question: This systematic review examines whether children with gender and sexual minority parents (LGBTQ parents) experience more mental health problems compared to children with different-sex parents, and evaluates the methodological rigor of studies conducted between 2015 and 2022 on this topic.

comparison: General population or non-anxiety disorder controls (implied reference for prevalence comparison)
exposure: Anxiety disorders (PTSD, OCD, social phobia/social anxiety disorder, panic disorder)
outcome: Prevalence of erectile dysfunction and severity of ED symptoms (measured by International Index of Erectile Function-5 scores)
population: Adult males with diagnosed anxiety disorders (including PTSD, OCD, social phobia/social anxiety disorder, and panic disorder)
research_question: This systematic review aims to define the prevalence and severity of erectile dysfunction in adult males diagnosed with anxiety disorders, including post-traumatic stress disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder, social phobia/social anxiety disorder, and panic disorder.

comparison: Pre-operative baseline function or standard functional benchmarks
intervention: Glansectomy with or without neoglans reconstruction
outcome: Functional outcomes including erectile function preservation, sexual activity, voiding ability while standing, glans sensation, meatal stenosis, graft loss, cosmetic satisfaction, recurrence rate, and disease-specific survival
population: Patients with localized penile cancer confined to the glans penis
research_question: This systematic review evaluates the functional outcomes, including sexual function, urinary function, and quality of life, following glansectomy with or without neoglans reconstruction in patients with localized penile cancer confined to the glans penis.

comparison: No specific comparison group; review synthesizes available evidence on HFS presentations and treatments
exposure: Hard-flaccid syndrome, potentially triggered by penile trauma causing neurovascular and inflammatory events
outcome: Aetiopathogenesis understanding, clinical symptoms (perineal pain, urinary disturbances, erectile and ejaculatory dysfunction), diagnostic criteria, and treatment effectiveness (including PDE5 inhibitors, anxiolytics, low-intensity shockwave therapy, pelvic floor physical therapy, spinal surgery, and biopsychosocial therapy)
population: Male patients with hard-flaccid syndrome (HFS), a condition characterized by a semi-rigid penis in the flaccid state with associated erectile, urinary, ejaculatory, perineal and psychological symptoms
research_question: This systematic review aims to summarize the current understanding of hard-flaccid syndrome (HFS), including its aetiopathogenesis, clinical presentation, diagnostic approaches, and management strategies in male patients presenting with this rare condition characterized by a semi-rigid penis in the flaccid state.

comparison: Pre-operative status (before LVSG surgery)
intervention: Laparoscopic vertical sleeve gastrectomy (LVSG)
outcome: Lower esophageal sphincter pressure (LESP), lower esophageal sphincter length (LESL), DeMeester Score (DMS), and BMI change
population: Patients with morbid obesity undergoing laparoscopic vertical sleeve gastrectomy
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates the impact of laparoscopic vertical sleeve gastrectomy (LVSG) on lower esophageal sphincter pressure (LESP), lower esophageal sphincter length (LESL), and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) as measured by DeMeester Score in patients with morbid obesity, comparing pre-operative and post-operative esophageal function test data.

comparison: Non-PCOS healthy controls; women with smaller neck circumference
exposure: Neck circumference (NC) as an anthropometric marker of upper body adiposity
outcome: Neck circumference values, metabolic syndrome prevalence, insulin resistance (HOMA-IR, HOMA%S, fasting insulin), anthropometric measurements (waist circumference, hip circumference), blood pressure, lipid values (triglycerides), and glucose metabolism parameters
population: Women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigates whether women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) have larger neck circumference compared to non-PCOS controls, and examines the associations between neck circumference and metabolic abnormalities including metabolic syndrome and insulin resistance among women with PCOS.

comparison: Waitlist or standard care conditions
intervention: Online, group-based behavior change interventions for weight management
outcome: Weight loss, weight-related behavior changes, and user perceptions of acceptability, usability, and overall experience
population: Adults with severe obesity (BMI ≥ 35 kg/m²)
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis examines the effectiveness of online, group-based behavior change interventions for adults with severe obesity (BMI ≥ 35 kg/m²) in achieving weight loss and positive health behavior changes compared to waitlist or standard care conditions, while also exploring user perceptions of acceptability and usability.

comparison: Control groups (standard protocol/placebo without probiotics)
intervention: Probiotic supplementation
outcome: Liver function (aspartate aminotransferase levels), lipid metabolism (triglycerides), body weight, vitamin B12 levels, dietary intake (energy, protein, carbohydrate, fiber), and safety/side effects
population: Patients with morbid obesity undergoing bariatric surgery
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigates whether probiotic supplementation improves clinical outcomes, including liver function (AST levels), lipid metabolism (triglycerides), weight loss, vitamin B12 levels, and dietary intake parameters, in patients with morbid obesity undergoing bariatric surgery compared to control groups receiving standard care or placebo.

comparison: Lower PFAS exposure levels or non-exposed reference groups
exposure: Prenatal and postnatal exposure to perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), including PFOA and PFOS
outcome: Pediatric obesity measures including body mass index (BMI), BMI z-score, and waist circumference
population: Children up to 12 years of age
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis examines whether prenatal and postnatal exposure to perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) is associated with pediatric obesity in children up to 12 years of age, exploring heterogeneity by chemical type and exposure timing.

comparison: Gender responsiveness categories (gender unequal vs gender unaware) according to WHO Gender Responsiveness Assessment Scale
intervention: Water, sanitation and/or handwashing with soap interventions
outcome: Women's engagement in research activities, women's engagement in intervention activities, time burden reporting, gender responsiveness classification, and assessment of intervention impacts specific to women
population: Studies from systematic reviews assessing WASH interventions on diarrhoeal disease and acute respiratory infections in low- and middle-income countries
research_question: This systematic re-review examines how women are engaged in water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) research and intervention activities in low- and middle-income countries, specifically assessing the gender of individuals engaged in these activities, whether time burdens were reported and compensated, whether impacts specific to women were evaluated, and how gender-responsive the interventions were according to the WHO Gender Responsiveness Assessment Scale.

comparison: Comparison across different evaluation approaches, privacy metrics versus utility metrics, and assessment of whether privacy protection is adequately addressed relative to utility
exposure: Methods and metrics used for evaluating privacy and utility of synthetic medical data
outcome: Consensus on evaluation methods for synthetic data, balance between privacy and utility assessment, identification of gaps in privacy evaluation practices
population: Studies evaluating synthetic health-related or medical data
research_question: This scoping review examines whether there is consensus within the research community on standardized methods for evaluating the privacy and utility of synthetic health-related data, and whether privacy considerations are given equal importance as utility when assessing synthetic medical data.

comparison: Incomplete cytoreductive surgery (CRS)
intervention: Complete or optimal cytoreductive surgery (CRS)
outcome: Overall survival (OS)
population: Patients with primary stage IV endometrial cancer
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigates whether complete or optimal cytoreductive surgery (CRS) improves overall survival compared to incomplete CRS in patients with primary stage IV endometrial cancer.

comparison: Comparisons across years of publication and between different drug classes
intervention: Experimental compounds as single agents or in combination with dexamethasone in phase I and phase II clinical trials
outcome: Overall response rate (ORR) and toxicity
population: Patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM)
research_question: This meta-analysis examines the therapeutic outcomes, specifically overall response rates and toxicity profiles, of early-phase (phase I and phase II) clinical trials investigating experimental drugs as single agents or in combination with dexamethasone in patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma over the past decade.

comparison: Mammography alone
intervention: Mammography supplemented with ultrasound screening
outcome: Proportion of cancers detected only by ultrasound, additional screen-detected cancer cases per 1000 mammography-negative women, and referral rates for diagnostic assessment
population: Women with dense breast tissue undergoing breast cancer screening
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigates whether adding ultrasound screening to mammography improves breast cancer detection rates in women with dense breast tissue compared to mammography alone, and examines the impact on referral rates for diagnostic assessment.

comparison: standard chemotherapy or control treatment
intervention: anti-EGFR monoclonal antibody therapy
outcome: overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS)
population: patients with RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether BRAF V600E mutation status is predictive of treatment benefit from anti-EGFR monoclonal antibody therapy in patients with RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer compared to those without BRAF mutations.

comparison: Lowest/bottom category of alcohol intake (non-drinkers or minimal drinkers)
exposure: Alcoholic beverage intake (total alcohol, beer, wine, and liquor consumption)
outcome: Renal cell cancer risk (measured as relative risk)
population: General adult population (participants from case-control and cohort studies examining renal cell cancer)
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether alcoholic beverage intake (including total alcohol, beer, wine, and liquor) is associated with the risk of renal cell cancer, and examines whether this association differs by sex, study design, and level of consumption.

comparison: Lowest category of serum PLP levels, dietary vitamin B6 intake, serum vitamin B12 levels, dietary vitamin B12 intake, and dietary methionine intake
exposure: Vitamin B6 (serum pyridoxal 5'-phosphate levels and dietary intake), vitamin B12 (serum levels and dietary intake), and methionine (dietary intake)
outcome: Breast cancer risk (relative risk)
population: Women (including pre-menopausal and post-menopausal women)
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether vitamin B6 (serum PLP levels and dietary intake), vitamin B12 (serum levels and dietary intake), and methionine (dietary intake) are associated with breast cancer risk in women, and examines the dose-response relationship between these one-carbon metabolism nutrients and breast cancer risk, with particular attention to differences between pre-menopausal and post-menopausal women.

comparison: Biomarkers validated in single studies versus those validated in at least two independent publications
exposure: Biomarker expression levels (IL-6, IL-8, Prolactin in liquid samples; HIF-1α, SOX2, E-cadherin, vimentin, MALAT1, TP53, and NOTCH1 in tissue biopsies)
outcome: Clinical relevance for early diagnosis and prognosis prediction of TSCC, including diagnostic accuracy and prognostic value
population: Patients with tongue squamous cell carcinoma (TSCC)
research_question: This systematic review examines which biomarkers show consistent clinical relevance for early diagnosis and prognosis prediction of tongue squamous cell carcinoma (TSCC), comparing biomarkers validated in at least two independent studies across different sample sources including body fluids (saliva, serum/plasma) and tissue biopsies.

comparison: Non-statin users
exposure: Statin use (including lipophilic and hydrophilic statins)
outcome: Breast cancer-specific death (BCD) and breast cancer recurrence (BCR)
population: Breast cancer patients
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigates the association between statin use and breast cancer-specific mortality and recurrence in breast cancer patients, with particular attention to potential effect modifiers including immortal time bias, statin type (lipophilic vs hydrophilic), estrogen receptor status, cancer stage, and type of postdiagnostic use.

comparison: Digital mammography (DM) screening
intervention: Digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT) screening
outcome: Cancer detection rate (CDR) and recall rate, specifically the incremental differences between DBT and DM stratified by breast density
population: Women undergoing population breast cancer screening with varying breast densities (high-density/dense breasts versus low-density/non-dense breasts, classified by BI-RADS)
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis examines whether digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT) detects breast cancer differentially compared to digital mammography (DM) in women with high-density versus low-density breasts during population screening, specifically evaluating differences in cancer detection rate and recall rate by breast density.

comparison: Non-users of bisphosphonates
exposure: Bisphosphonate use (including nitrogen-containing and non-nitrogen-containing bisphosphonates, with consideration of duration of use)
outcome: Risk of cancers (all-cause cancer and specific cancer types including colorectal, breast, endometrial, liver, and pancreatic cancer)
population: General population, including bisphosphonate users (primarily patients with osteoporosis or bone-related conditions)
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigates whether the use of bisphosphonates is associated with the risk of overall cancers and individual types of cancers, and further examines whether different types (nitrogen-containing vs. non-nitrogen-containing) and duration of bisphosphonate use influence cancer risk compared to non-users.

comparison: Biennial mammography screening (as the reference interval for comparing annual and triennial screening)
intervention: Annual, biennial, or triennial mammography screening
outcome: Breast cancer deaths averted, quality-adjusted life years (QALYs), breast cancer stage at detection, interval cancers, overdiagnosis, false positive results, and radiation-related effects
population: Women at average risk of breast cancer aged 45-74 years (subgroups: 45-49, 50-69, and 70-74 years)
research_question: This systematic review examines the benefits and harms of different mammography screening intervals (annual, biennial, or triennial) for breast cancer detection in women at average risk of breast cancer across different age groups (45-49, 50-69, and 70-74 years), comparing outcomes such as breast cancer deaths averted, quality-adjusted life years, cancer stage at detection, interval cancers, overdiagnosis, and false positive results.

comparison: No interceptive treatment or delayed treatment
intervention: Extraction of the primary canine as interceptive treatment
outcome: Normalization of eruptive position and successful eruption of the palatally displaced maxillary canine
population: Children aged 10-13 years with palatally displaced maxillary canines in the mixed dentition
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether extraction of the primary canine as an interceptive treatment promotes eruption and normalizes the eruptive position of palatally displaced maxillary canines in children aged 10-13 years in the mixed dentition, compared to no intervention or delayed treatment.

comparison: other teaching pedagogies (traditional didactic teaching methods such as lectures, problem-based learning, enquiry-based learning, case-based learning)
intervention: team-based learning (TBL)
outcome: student satisfaction and student academic performance
population: undergraduate dental students
research_question: This scoping review investigates whether team-based learning (TBL) is an effective alternative teaching pedagogy compared to other teaching methods (including traditional didactic teaching and other dialectic approaches) for delivering undergraduate dental education, examining outcomes related to student satisfaction and academic performance.

comparison: Non-exposed individuals or settings without sexual misconduct incidents
exposure: Sexual misconduct behaviors including unwelcome sexual advances, comments, gestures, and physical contact in dental settings
outcome: Prevalence of sexual misconduct, underreporting rates, emotional trauma, professional disengagement, and effectiveness of interventions targeting sexual misconduct behaviors
population: Dental practitioners, dental office staff, patients, students, and educators in dental care settings
research_question: This systematic review explores the prevalence, causes, impacts, and interventions related to sexual misconduct in dental care settings, examining how dental practitioners, staff, patients, and students experience inappropriate sexual behaviors in the dental workplace.

comparison: Expert clinical diagnosis or reference standard diagnosis of pathological myopia
exposure: Artificial intelligence-based diagnostic tools (particularly deep learning-based methods) for image analysis
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy measures including sensitivity, specificity, area under the summary receiver operator curve (SROC), and diagnostic odds ratio (DOR)
population: Eyes/patients undergoing screening or diagnosis for pathological myopia using colour fundus photography
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis assesses the diagnostic accuracy of artificial intelligence-based methods for the detection of pathological myopia using colour fundus images, evaluating their sensitivity and specificity compared to expert clinical diagnosis.

comparison: Healthy subjects without glaucoma
exposure: Translaminar pressure difference (TPD = IOP – ICP)
outcome: Translaminar pressure difference levels and structural glaucomatous changes of the optic disc
population: Patients with open-angle glaucoma and healthy control subjects
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether translaminar pressure difference (TPD), defined as the difference between intraocular pressure and intracranial pressure, is elevated in patients with open-angle glaucoma compared to healthy subjects, and whether TPD is associated with structural glaucomatous changes of the optic disc.

comparison: DECIDE-AI checklist reporting standards (27-item checklist including 17 AI-specific items and 10 generic reporting items)
exposure: AI decision support systems for glaucoma diagnosis and progression identification
outcome: DECIDE-AI checklist adherence scores including AI-Specific Score, Generic-Item Score, and overall DECIDE-AI Score
population: Published studies reporting early clinical evaluation of AI decision support systems for glaucoma diagnosis or progression detection
research_question: This systematic review evaluates the quality of reporting in early clinical evaluation studies of artificial intelligence decision support systems for glaucoma diagnosis and progression detection, specifically assessing adherence to the DECIDE-AI checklist standards.

comparison: different menstrual cycle phases (follicular vs luteal) and pre- vs post-menopausal status
exposure: menstrual cycle phases and menopausal status
outcome: posterior pole structural parameters (macular morphology, choroidal thickness, optic disc characteristics)
population: healthy adult non-pregnant women from menarche to post-menopause
research_question: This scoping review examines the associations between posterior pole structures (macula, choroid, and optic disc) and hormonal fluctuations across women's reproductive life stages, including menstrual cycle phases and the post-menopausal period, in healthy adult non-pregnant women not using hormonal contraception or replacement therapy.

comparison: Comparison across different FST methodological approaches, testing parameters, and reporting standards used by various clinical centers
exposure: Full-field stimulus threshold (FST) testing methodology variations, including parameters such as flash luminance units, color, duration, test strategy, and dark adaptation protocols
outcome: Whole-field retinal light sensitivity threshold, variability in FST methodology reporting, and identification of gaps in standardized testing guidance
population: Patients with severe retinal disease, particularly inherited retinal disease (IRD), including pediatric populations
research_question: This scoping review examines the current variability in full-field stimulus threshold (FST) testing methodology and reporting practices across studies involving patients with severe retinal disease, with the aim of identifying gaps and informing standardized guidance for FST measurement.

comparison: lower PFOS exposure levels
exposure: perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS) biomarker concentrations
outcome: birth weight (in grams)
population: pregnant women and their newborns
research_question: This meta-analysis examines the association between maternal and neonatal biomarker concentrations of perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS) and birth weight deficits, investigating whether exposure to this legacy chemical is associated with reduced birth weight across different study designs and biomarker sampling approaches.

comparison: Non-exposed or control conditions (unexposed cells, sham-exposed subjects, or unexposed population groups)
exposure: Low-level radiofrequency electromagnetic fields above 6 GHz (millimetre waves) at exposure levels below ICNIRP occupational limits, including 5G network frequencies and radar emissions
outcome: Biological and health effects including genotoxicity, cell proliferation, gene expression, cell signalling, membrane function, cancer at different sites, reproductive effects, and other diseases
population: Humans, human cells, and biological systems (including in vitro cell models, in vivo animal models, and human populations in epidemiological studies)
research_question: This state-of-the-science review examines whether low-level radiofrequency (RF) fields above 6 GHz, such as those used by 5G mobile networks, cause adverse biological or health effects in humans and biological systems compared to non-exposed conditions, with outcomes including genotoxicity, cell proliferation, gene expression, cancer, reproductive effects, and other diseases.

comparison: Control conditions (standard care or no biofeedback intervention)
intervention: Biofeedback (including various modalities such as heart rate variability biofeedback)
outcome: Blood pressure changes (systolic and diastolic blood pressure)
population: Patients with hypertension
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to assess the effectiveness of biofeedback interventions on blood pressure reduction in patients with hypertension compared to control conditions.

comparison: Placebo or other antihypertensive treatments (ACE inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers, diuretics)
intervention: Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA) therapy
outcome: Blood pressure reduction (systolic and diastolic blood pressure) and safety/tolerability
population: Adults with low-renin hypertension
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigates whether mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA) therapy is effective and safe for lowering blood pressure in adults with low-renin hypertension compared to placebo or other antihypertensive treatments such as ACE inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers, and diuretics.

comparison: Different blood pressure measurement methods (24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring versus other methods of blood pressure measurement)
exposure: Turner syndrome (chromosomal disorder with partial or complete absence of one X chromosome)
outcome: Prevalence of hypertension
population: Paediatric patients with Turner syndrome aged 18 years or younger
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to determine the prevalence of hypertension in paediatric patients with Turner syndrome (aged 18 years or younger) and to explore the associated methodologies of blood pressure evaluation reported in these studies, including comparison between 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring and other measurement methods.

comparison: Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) alone
intervention: Renal denervation (RDN) combined with pulmonary vein isolation (PVI)
outcome: Atrial fibrillation recurrence, systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and complication rate
population: Hypertensive patients with atrial fibrillation
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether adding renal denervation (RDN) to pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) improves clinical outcomes including atrial fibrillation recurrence, blood pressure control, and estimated glomerular filtration rate in hypertensive patients with atrial fibrillation compared to PVI alone.

comparison: Baseline measurements (pre-intervention values)
intervention: Renal denervation (RDN) using endovascular catheter-based radiofrequency ablation of renal nerves
outcome: Office and ambulatory blood pressure (systolic and diastolic), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), serum creatinine levels, and procedural complication rates
population: Hypertensive patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and treatment-resistant hypertension
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates whether renal denervation (RDN) is safe and effective in reducing blood pressure and preserving kidney function in hypertensive patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) compared to baseline measurements over follow-up periods of 6, 12, and 24 months.

comparison: Lower sodium intake groups or recommended intake levels (below 5 g/day salt or 2 g/day sodium)
exposure: Dietary salt/sodium intake levels
outcome: Health outcomes including blood pressure, cardiovascular disease, physical performance, composite renal outcomes, chronic kidney disease, osteoporosis, and all-cause mortality
population: General adult population
research_question: This systematic review examines the association between dietary salt/sodium intake and various health outcomes, including blood pressure, cardiovascular disease, physical performance, renal outcomes, chronic kidney disease, osteoporosis, and all-cause mortality in the general adult population.

comparison: Non-exercise control conditions
intervention: Exercise training (including endurance training and various exercise modalities)
outcome: Plasma renin activity, angiotensin-II, aldosterone, epinephrine, norepinephrine, 24-hour urinary sodium and potassium excretion, systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, and heart rate
population: Adults with various health conditions including hypertension and healthy individuals
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates the effect of exercise training on the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) components, including plasma renin activity, angiotensin-II, aldosterone, epinephrine, norepinephrine, urinary sodium and potassium excretion, as well as blood pressure and heart rate, in adults with various health conditions including hypertension, compared to non-exercise control conditions.

comparison: Placebo-assisted psychotherapy or control conditions
intervention: MDMA-assisted psychotherapy (MDMA-AP)
outcome: Side effects and adverse events (including any side effect during medication sessions, side effects in the 7 days following sessions, and adverse events during treatment period)
population: Patients with psychiatric illness (including PTSD, terminal illness, depression, and other psychiatric conditions) receiving MDMA-assisted psychotherapy
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates the side effects and safety profile of MDMA-assisted psychotherapy across psychiatric indications compared to control conditions (placebo-assisted psychotherapy or other control conditions), examining adverse events during medication sessions, in the 7 days following sessions, and throughout the treatment period.

comparison: Placebo or control conditions
intervention: Melatonin supplements and melatonin receptor agonists (including tasimelteon and ramelteon)
outcome: Sleep-wake cycle parameters (sleep onset latency, total sleep time, wake after sleep onset) and circadian rhythm measures (dim-light melatonin onset, phase shifts, sleep timing)
population: Healthy participants and patients with psychiatric disorders (including bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, major depressive disorder, and other psychiatric conditions)
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigates whether melatonin supplements and melatonin receptor agonists can modulate sleep-wake cycles and circadian rhythms in healthy participants and patients with psychiatric disorders compared to placebo or control conditions, with particular focus on phase-shifting effects according to dosing time and dosage.

comparison: Placebo or sham treatment
intervention: Various antidepressant treatments including electroconvulsive therapy (ECT), minocycline, theta-burst stimulation (TBS), repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), ketamine, aripiprazole, and other pharmacological and neuromodulatory treatments (25 separate treatments total)
outcome: Response rate (primary outcome), with treatment effects measured as odds ratios
population: Adults with treatment-resistant depression who have not responded to at least two antidepressant trials, excluding those with bipolar or psychotic depression
research_question: This network meta-analysis compares the relative effectiveness of different antidepressant treatments, including pharmacological agents (such as ketamine, aripiprazole, and minocycline) and neuromodulatory procedures (such as electroconvulsive therapy, repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation, and theta-burst stimulation), in adults with treatment-resistant depression who have not responded to at least two antidepressant trials, with response rate as the primary outcome measure.

comparison: No thromboprophylaxis or standard care without anticoagulation
intervention: Primary thromboprophylaxis with minidose warfarin or low-dose low molecular weight heparin (LMWH)
outcome: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) incidence including symptomatic and asymptomatic CVC-related venous thrombosis, and bleeding complications
population: Cancer patients with indwelling central venous catheters (CVCs)
research_question: This systematic review examines whether primary thromboprophylaxis using minidose warfarin or low-dose low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) is effective in preventing venous thromboembolism in cancer patients with indwelling central venous catheters compared to no prophylaxis, and evaluates the associated bleeding risks.

comparison: healthy controls
exposure: major depressive disorder (medication-free)
outcome: cortical thickness (measured by MRI)
population: medication-free patients with major depressive disorder
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether medication-free patients with major depressive disorder show alterations in cortical thickness measured by MRI compared to healthy controls, and whether these alterations are associated with demographic and clinical characteristics.

comparison: Brief-pulse electroconvulsive therapy (pulse width 0.5-1.5 milliseconds) or conventional ECT
intervention: Ultrabrief pulse electroconvulsive therapy (pulse width <0.5 milliseconds)
outcome: Remission rates, response rates, relapse rates, and switching rates to other forms of ECT
population: Patients with depression receiving electroconvulsive therapy
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to assess acute and long-term outcomes following ultrabrief pulse electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) for depression, including remission rates, response rates, relapse rates, and switching rates to other forms of ECT, compared to conventional brief-pulse ECT.

comparison: Baseline (pre-treatment) BDNF levels or placebo/control conditions
intervention: Administration of psychoplastogens (ketamine, esketamine, LSD, psilocybin, ayahuasca, DMT, MDMA, scopolamine, and rapastinel)
outcome: Peripheral blood levels of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) measured in serum or plasma
population: Human subjects including both healthy individuals and patients with psychiatric diagnoses
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether psychoplastogens (including ketamine, esketamine, LSD, psilocybin, ayahuasca, DMT, MDMA, scopolamine, and rapastinel) elevate peripheral blood levels of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) in humans compared to baseline or control conditions, testing whether the rapid upregulation of neuroplasticity observed in preclinical studies is detectable using peripheral BDNF as a biomarker.

comparison: placebo
intervention: antidepressants (20 different types including agomelatine, amitriptyline, bupropion, citalopram, desvenlafaxine, duloxetine, escitalopram, fluoxetine, fluvoxamine, levomilnacipran, milnacipran, mirtazapine, nefazodone, paroxetine, reboxetine, sertraline, tianeptine, venlafaxine, vilazodone, and vortioxetine)
outcome: 6-month relapse rate (primary), all-cause discontinuation, discontinuation due to adverse events, and incidence of individual adverse events
population: adults with major depressive disorder in the maintenance phase (stabilized on antidepressants)
research_question: This systematic review and network meta-analysis investigates the efficacy, acceptability, tolerability, and safety of various antidepressants compared to placebo for maintaining remission in adults with major depressive disorder who have been stabilized on antidepressant treatment during the maintenance phase.

comparison: Within-patient correlational analysis (no separate control group; associations examined within patient samples)
exposure: Blood-based immune markers including pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory indices, inflammatory cytokines, kynurenine metabolites, and markers of microglial activation
outcome: Global cognitive performance and domain-specific cognitive functioning across eight cognitive domains
population: Patients with schizophrenia spectrum disorder, bipolar disorder, or major depressive disorder
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates the association between blood-based immune markers (including inflammatory cytokines, kynurenine metabolites, and markers of microglial activation) and cognitive dysfunction in patients with psychotic and mood disorders, including schizophrenia spectrum disorder, bipolar disorder, and major depressive disorder.

comparison: Switching to placebo (discontinuation of antidepressant)
intervention: Continuation of the same antidepressant medication used to achieve remission (maintenance therapy)
outcome: Relapse rate, treatment failure, all-cause dropout, tolerability (acceptability)
population: Patients with major depressive disorder who achieved remission with antidepressant medication during acute treatment
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether continuing antidepressant medication after achieving remission reduces the risk of relapse and treatment failure in patients with major depressive disorder compared to switching to placebo, while also examining the influence of various clinical factors including antidepressant class, dosing schedule, duration of maintenance treatment, and patient age.

comparison: Different clinical stages of Alzheimer's disease (preclinical, MCI, mild/moderate/severe dementia) and cognitively normal controls
exposure: Neuroinflammatory fluid biomarker levels (YKL-40, sTREM2, and GFAP) in cerebrospinal fluid and plasma
outcome: Association with AD clinical stage, disease progression, and long-term clinical outcomes including cognitive decline
population: Patients with preclinical Alzheimer's disease, mild cognitive impairment (MCI) due to AD, and AD dementia
research_question: This systematic literature review investigates the association between neuroinflammatory fluid biomarkers (YKL-40, sTREM2, and GFAP) and clinical stages of Alzheimer's disease, and examines whether changes in these biomarkers can predict long-term clinical outcomes such as cognitive decline in patients across the AD continuum, from preclinical stages through MCI to dementia.

comparison: Thick gingival phenotype
exposure: Gingival phenotype (thin vs. thick)
outcome: Implant survival rate, marginal bone loss, peri-implantitis incidence, and clinical parameters
population: Patients with dental implants
research_question: This systematic review investigates whether gingival phenotype (thick or thin) influences dental implant survival rate and marginal bone loss around dental implants, examining whether thin gingival phenotype is associated with increased risk of peri-implantitis and unfavorable clinical outcomes compared to thick gingival phenotype.

comparison: Unhealthy or Western diet (high in refined carbohydrates, high in saturated fats, low in fibre, and low in nutritional value) or standard dietary habits
intervention: Adoption of a healthy diet (Mediterranean, Optimised, Okinawan, or Low Inflammatory diet - characterized as low in refined carbohydrates, low in saturated fats, high in fibre, and high in nutritional value)
outcome: Periodontal parameters (measures of gingivitis and periodontitis severity)
population: Patients with periodontal diseases (gingivitis or periodontitis)
research_question: This systematic review investigates whether adopting a healthy diet (low in refined carbohydrates, low in saturated fats, high in fibre, and high in nutritional value) improves periodontal parameters in patients with periodontal diseases (gingivitis or periodontitis) compared to those following an unhealthy or Western diet.

comparison: Individuals without periodontitis or without the specific noncommunicable disease being studied
exposure: Periodontitis (when examining NCDs as outcome) or noncommunicable diseases (when examining periodontitis as outcome)
outcome: Development or progression of noncommunicable diseases (cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, respiratory diseases, malignancies, and other NCDs) and periodontitis, measured by odds ratio, risk ratio, or hazard ratio
population: Individuals with periodontitis and/or noncommunicable diseases
research_question: This umbrella review synthesizes and grades the strength and certainty of scientific evidence regarding the bidirectional association between periodontitis and noncommunicable diseases (NCDs), examining whether periodontitis serves as a risk factor for NCDs such as cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, and respiratory diseases, and conversely, whether these NCDs influence the development or progression of periodontitis.

comparison: Breast milk or expressed breast milk (BM/EBM)
intervention: Sucrose (24%) or glucose (30%, 10%, 25%) administration
outcome: Pain intensity measured by Premature Infant Pain Profile (PIPP/PIPP-R) scores, crying duration, heart rate change, and adverse events
population: Preterm infants (born less than 37 weeks of gestation) requiring heel lancing and venipuncture procedures
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigates whether sucrose or glucose is more effective than breast milk or expressed breast milk for pain control and reducing crying duration in preterm infants undergoing heel lancing and venipuncture procedures.

comparison: Standard care or control group without home visits by community health workers
intervention: Home visits by trained community health workers (CHWs)
outcome: Identification of serious illness (sensitivity and specificity) and care seeking from health facilities
population: Newborns and young infants up to 59 days of age from low- and middle-income countries
research_question: This meta-analysis evaluates whether home visits by trained community health workers (CHWs) improve the identification of serious illness and increase care seeking from health facilities in newborns and young infants (up to 59 days of age) from low- and middle-income countries compared to standard care without home visits.

comparison: Offspring of women without polycystic ovary syndrome
exposure: Maternal polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) diagnosis
outcome: Birth outcomes including preterm birth, fetal growth restriction, low birth weight, mean birthweight, small for gestational age, admission to neonatal intensive care units, and perinatal mortality
population: Offspring of women with and without polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigates whether polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is an independent risk factor for adverse birth outcomes in offspring of affected women, examining the association between maternal PCOS status and birth outcomes while considering potential confounders such as maternal age, BMI, and use of assisted reproductive technology.

comparison: Treatment as usual (standard antipsychotic prescribing without pharmacogenetic testing)
intervention: Pharmacogenetics-guided prescribing of antipsychotics based on genetic testing (e.g., CYP450 gene panel testing to determine metabolic phenotypes)
outcome: Clinical outcomes (treatment response, adverse drug reactions, symptom severity, treatment resistance, medication adherence) and economic outcomes (healthcare costs, resource utilization, cost-effectiveness)
population: Individuals undergoing antipsychotic treatment, including patients with psychotic disorders such as schizophrenia
research_question: This systematic review investigates whether pharmacogenetic testing in individuals undergoing antipsychotic treatment influences clinical outcomes (such as treatment response, adverse drug reactions, and symptom severity) or economic outcomes (such as healthcare costs and resource utilization) compared to treatment as usual without genetic testing.

comparison: Healthy controls
exposure: Presence of schizophrenia diagnosis
outcome: Syntactic comprehension and production performance measured by Cohen's d effect sizes and log coefficient of variation ratio across 6 domains (2 comprehension, 4 production)
population: Adults (≥18 years) with schizophrenia
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates the nature and extent of syntactic deficits in individuals with schizophrenia compared to healthy controls, examining both syntax comprehension and production abilities across multiple domains to quantify the degree and interindividual variability of grammatical impairments.

comparison: Placebo/sham treatment, conservative treatment options, and pairwise comparisons between all treatment modalities
intervention: Neuromodulation (mainly Spinal Cord Stimulation), minimally invasive treatments (predominantly epidural injections), conservative treatments (physiotherapy, cognitive training, and medication), and reoperation
outcome: Pain intensity (measured as standardized mean differences)
population: Patients with Persistent Spinal Pain Syndrome Type 2 (PSPS-T2), defined as patients experiencing chronic spinal pain despite previous spinal surgery
research_question: This systematic review and network meta-analysis compares the effectiveness of different treatment modalities, including neuromodulation (particularly Spinal Cord Stimulation), minimally invasive treatments (such as epidural injections), conservative treatments (physiotherapy, cognitive training, and medication), and reoperation, for reducing pain intensity in patients with Persistent Spinal Pain Syndrome Type 2 (PSPS-T2, previously known as Failed Back Surgery Syndrome).

comparison: Comparison across time periods (pre-2022 vs. 2022 onwards) and geographic regions (endemic vs. nonendemic countries)
exposure: Mpox virus infection
outcome: Proportion of women among confirmed mpox cases
population: Confirmed mpox (monkeypox) cases, with focus on women including cis and trans women
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to estimate the proportion of women among mpox (monkeypox) cases across various settings and outbreaks, and to examine how the sex distribution of mpox patients varies by time period (before 2022 vs. 2022 onwards) and geographic region (endemic vs. nonendemic countries).

comparison: Higher intelligence levels within the study populations
exposure: Lower intelligence (IQ) as measured by standardized intelligence tests in early life
outcome: Risk of later-life physical illness (e.g., diabetes, arthritis, stroke) and mental illness (e.g., schizophrenia, depression, dementia, bipolar disorder)
population: General population with intelligence test scores obtained in childhood, adolescence, or early adulthood (under 21 years of age), excluding clinical populations without healthy controls
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether lower intelligence (IQ) measured in early life (childhood, adolescence, or early adulthood before age 21) is associated with an increased risk of developing physical and mental health disorders in later life, and examines how this association varies across different health conditions and is moderated by factors such as education and healthcare quality.

comparison: Healthy control subjects, and in some analyses, individuals with unipolar depression or schizophrenia
exposure: Bipolar disorder diagnosis (including different mood states: mania, depression, euthymia)
outcome: Basal free intracellular calcium ion concentrations ([Ca2+]) in platelets and lymphocytes, and stimulated [Ca2+] response to 5-HT or thrombin
population: Individuals with bipolar disorder
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis examines whether intracellular calcium ion concentrations and calcium signalling parameters are altered in individuals with bipolar disorder compared to healthy controls, and whether these alterations differ across mood states (mania, depression, euthymia) and from other psychiatric conditions.

comparison: Individuals without elevated biomarker levels or those who did not develop MDD
exposure: Biological biomarkers including neuroimaging measures (brain volumes), gastrointestinal factors, immunology markers, neurotrophic factors, neurotransmitters, hormones (particularly cortisol), and oxidative stress markers
outcome: Onset, relapse, or recurrence of major depressive disorder (MDD) diagnosed via clinical interview, and time until MDD onset/relapse/recurrence
population: Individuals at risk for major depressive disorder (MDD), including those with no prior history and those with previous MDD episodes
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigates whether biological biomarkers derived from leading theories (including neuroimaging, gastrointestinal factors, immunology, neurotrophic factors, neurotransmitters, hormones, and oxidative stress) can prospectively predict the onset, relapse, or recurrence of major depressive disorder (MDD) in individuals at risk compared to those without such biomarker alterations.

comparison: Placebo or standard treatments
intervention: L-type calcium channel antagonists (verapamil, diltiazem, nimodipine, nifedipine, methyoxyverapamil, isradipine)
outcome: Treatment efficacy for acute manic and depressive episodes, relapse prevention, and tolerability
population: Patients with bipolar disorder
research_question: This systematic review examines whether L-type calcium channel (LTCC) antagonists (including verapamil, diltiazem, nimodipine, nifedipine, methyoxyverapamil, and isradipine) are effective for the treatment of acute episodes (manic and depressive) and prevention of relapse in patients with bipolar disorder compared to placebo or standard treatments.

comparison: Healthy controls (non-schizophrenic postmortem brain samples)
exposure: Schizophrenia diagnosis
outcome: Neuroinflammatory markers including microglial markers, glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) expression, glial cell densities, cytokines, arachidonic cascade markers, substance P, SERPINA3, and IFITM
population: Postmortem brain samples from schizophrenia patients
research_question: This systematic review examines the postmortem evidence of cerebral inflammation in schizophrenia by evaluating whether neuroinflammatory markers (including microglia, astrocytes, cytokines, and other inflammatory markers) are altered in postmortem brain samples from schizophrenia patients compared to healthy controls.

comparison: Drug-free baseline or control condition
intervention: Acute and chronic ketamine administration at sub-anaesthetic and anaesthetic doses
outcome: Dopamine levels in brain regions (cortex, striatum, nucleus accumbens, hippocampus, ventral pallidum, cerebellum) and dopamine neuron population activity
population: Rodents, non-human primates, and humans (brain tissue and in vivo measurements)
research_question: This meta-analysis examines whether acute and chronic ketamine administration at sub-anaesthetic doses affects dopamine levels in the brain of rodents, non-human primates, and humans compared to drug-free baseline or control conditions, with implications for understanding its role in neuropsychiatric disorders including substance abuse, schizophrenia, and depression.

comparison: People unexposed to agricultural land-use (those not living or working in agricultural areas)
exposure: Occupational or residential exposure to agricultural land-use (including oil palm, rubber, non-poultry livestock farming, crops, and pasture)
outcome: Infectious disease risk measured as infection prevalence (including hookworm, malaria, scrub typhus, spotted fever group diseases, and other pathogen infections)
population: People living or working in Southeast Asia (ASEAN region including Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos PDR, Thailand, Myanmar, Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore, Philippines, East Timor, and Brunei)
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether occupational or residential exposure to agricultural land-use is associated with increased infectious disease risk in humans in Southeast Asia, comparing those who live or work in agricultural land to unexposed populations.

comparison: Microplastics transported as individual entities versus microplastics incorporated into flocs
exposure: Microplastic size fractions and their physicochemical characteristics (shape, density, polymer type, surface properties)
outcome: Flocculation behavior of microplastics, specifically the size threshold for incorporation into flocs (<162 µm) and prediction of transport modes in aquatic environments
population: Microplastics in aquatic environments including freshwater (rivers, lakes, reservoirs), marine, and estuarine systems
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates which size fractions of microplastics can be incorporated into and transported by flocs in various aquatic environments, aiming to understand and predict the flocculation behavior of microplastics based on their size relationship with flocs.

comparison: Placebo or no intervention groups within ATI studies; comparison between early-ART and late-ART initiators
exposure: Analytical treatment interruption (ATI) of antiretroviral therapy, with stratification by timing of ART initiation (early-ART within 6 months of HIV acquisition vs. late-ART)
outcome: Time to viral rebound (plasma HIV RNA viral load >50, >400, and >10,000 copies/mL) and frequency of post-treatment control (pVL <50 copies/mL at day 84 post-ATI)
population: People with HIV (PWH) who underwent analytical treatment interruption, predominantly male (91%), white (75%), with median age of 42 years
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates the time to HIV viral rebound and the frequency of post-treatment control (PTC) after analytical treatment interruption (ATI) of antiretroviral therapy among people with HIV who received placebo or no intervention, and examines whether timing of ART initiation (early vs. late) influences viral rebound dynamics and PTC rates.

comparison: Different study designs (observational studies, Mendelian randomization, randomized controlled trials) with varying levels of salt exposure
exposure: Salt intake
outcome: Blood pressure, cardiovascular diseases, and cardiovascular deaths; additionally, performance metrics for LLM extraction including direction of effect (F1=0.86), statistical significance (F1=0.96), Convergency of Evidence (CoE), and Level of Convergency (LoC)
population: General population studied across various research designs including observational studies, Mendelian randomization studies, and randomized controlled trials
research_question: This study investigates whether large language models can effectively extract and synthesize causal evidence across diverse study designs (observational studies, Mendelian randomization, and randomized controlled trials) to automate evidence triangulation, using the relationship between salt intake and blood pressure/cardiovascular outcomes as a case study.

comparison: Non-TNBC breast cancer tissue microbiome
exposure: TNBC-associated breast tissue microbiome composition (presence and abundance of specific microbial taxa)
outcome: Microbial community composition differences, enrichment of specific genera and species (Azospirillum, Gemmiger formicilis, Anaerobutyricum soehngenii), and functional pathway involvement related to chronic inflammation, cellular proliferation, invasion, and metastasis
population: Breast cancer patients with tissue samples, specifically comparing TNBC patients to non-TNBC patients (200 samples across four independent cohorts)
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates the distinct microbial composition of breast tissue in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) patients compared to non-TNBC breast cancer patients, aiming to identify specific microbial species and their functional pathways that may contribute to the aggressiveness and poor prognosis characteristic of TNBC.

comparison: Non-stunted children (height-for-age within normal range)
exposure: Gut microbiome composition (including alpha diversity, beta diversity, taxonomic abundance at phylum and genus levels, and metabolic pathways)
outcome: Stunting status (height-for-age more than two standard deviations below the WHO child growth median)
population: Children under 5 years of age in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs)
research_question: This systematic review examines the associations between gut microbiome composition and stunting in children under 5 years of age in low- and middle-income countries, comparing microbial diversity, taxonomic abundance, and metabolic pathways between stunted and non-stunted children.

comparison: Healthy controls or normative time perception standards
exposure: Alzheimer's disease pathology affecting time perception mechanisms
outcome: Time perception distortions including prospective timing, retrospective timing, and perception of shorter and longer time intervals
population: Patients with Alzheimer's disease diagnosed according to NINCDS-ADRDA criteria
research_question: This systematic review examines how time perception is distorted in patients with Alzheimer's disease compared to healthy controls, and explores the theoretical relationship between time distortions and episodic memory impairment in AD.

comparison: Standard care or no intervention (control groups from randomised controlled trials)
intervention: Preconception or antenatal lifestyle interventions including exercise, diet, and physical activity programs
outcome: Offspring cardiac remodelling (cardiac structure including interventricular septal wall thickness, cardiac function including systolic and diastolic function), and related cardiovascular parameters (blood pressure, resting heart rate, arterial thickening/stiffness)
population: Offspring of pregnant women with obesity (children aged from less than 2 months to 3-7 years old)
research_question: This systematic review examines whether preconception or antenatal lifestyle interventions (including exercise, diet, and physical activity programs) in pregnant women with obesity can prevent or reduce offspring cardiac remodelling and improve related cardiovascular health parameters in children compared to standard care.

comparison: Control conditions in randomized controlled trials (standard care or no intervention)
intervention: Internet- and mobile-based interventions (IMI) delivered via web browser or smartphone app aimed at improving mental health
outcome: Depressive symptom severity and weight reduction
population: Adults with overweight (BMI ≥25) or obesity (BMI ≥30) experiencing comorbid depressive symptoms
research_question: This systematic review examines whether internet- and mobile-based interventions (IMI) are effective in reducing depressive symptom severity in adults with overweight or obesity who experience comorbid depressive symptoms, and evaluates the quality of available evidence for these interventions.

comparison: Control groups (randomized controlled trial comparators)
intervention: Digital health interventions for sleep, including digital cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (dCBT-I) and sleep promotion programs (education, hygiene, or holistic programs)
outcome: Insomnia severity, sleep quality, and mental health outcomes
population: Adolescents aged 10-24 years (mean age 19.0; 71% female)
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis examines the effectiveness and active components of digital health interventions (including digital cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia and sleep promotion programs) for improving sleep outcomes in adolescents aged 10-24 years compared to control conditions.

comparison: Usual care
intervention: Electronic health interventions including computerized decision-support systems (CDS), electronic health records (EHR), electronic medication administration records (eMAR), computerized physician order entry (CPOE), and barcode medication administration (BCMA)
outcome: Medication errors (including potential errors, actual errors, and adverse drug events)
population: Patients in healthcare settings including hospitals, clinics, and pharmacies
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether electronic health interventions, particularly computerized decision-support systems (CDS), are effective in reducing medication errors compared to usual care in healthcare settings.

comparison: Clinicians without AI assistance (same diagnostic task performed independently)
intervention: Deep learning-based AI assistance for skin cancer diagnosis
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy for skin cancer diagnosis, measured by sensitivity and specificity
population: Clinicians (medical professionals including dermatologists and non-dermatologists) diagnosing skin lesions for skin cancer
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigates whether deep learning-based AI assistance improves the diagnostic accuracy (sensitivity and specificity) of clinicians in skin cancer diagnosis compared to clinicians performing the same diagnostic task without AI assistance.

comparison: Centralized machine learning models trained on single-centre or aggregated data
intervention: Federated learning approaches for training machine learning models on distributed, multi-centre cancer data
outcome: Machine learning model generalizability, diagnostic performance, and clinical applicability in cancer detection, diagnosis, and precision medicine
population: Patients with breast, lung, or prostate cancer (data from multi-centre oncology studies)
research_question: This systematic review examines whether federated learning approaches improve machine learning model generalizability and performance in breast, lung, and prostate cancer research compared to traditional centralized machine learning methods, while addressing privacy-preserving collaborative training on multi-centre data.

comparison: Non-statin users (controls without statin exposure)
exposure: Statin exposure (including lipophilic and hydrophilic statins)
outcome: Incidence of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), all-cause mortality, cirrhosis, and cirrhosis decompensation
population: Individuals with chronic viral hepatitis (chronic hepatitis B and chronic hepatitis C)
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether statin exposure is associated with a reduced incidence of adverse events, including hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), all-cause mortality, cirrhosis, and cirrhosis decompensation, in individuals with chronic viral hepatitis (hepatitis B and C) compared to non-statin users.

comparison: Conventional exercises and no treatment
intervention: Technology-assisted rehabilitation including exergaming with balance platforms, exergaming with motion capture technologies, serious gaming, interventions with wearables, and telerehabilitation
outcome: Balance and functional mobility outcomes including clinical functional scales, functional mobility measures, and gait speed
population: Older adults aged 60 years and over
research_question: This network meta-analysis aims to evaluate and compare the effectiveness of technology-assisted rehabilitation interventions, including virtual reality exergaming (with balance platforms or motion capture), serious gaming, wearables, and telerehabilitation, on improving balance and functional mobility in older adults aged 60 and over, compared to conventional exercises or no treatment.

comparison: Usual care (standard clinical practice without automated alerting system)
intervention: Automated alerting system for sepsis detection (including rule-based and machine learning-based prediction methods)
outcome: Mortality and length of stay (LOS)
population: Hospitalized patients with sepsis
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether automated alerting systems for sepsis detection improve clinical outcomes, particularly mortality and length of stay, in patients with sepsis compared to usual care, and further examines whether effectiveness varies by clinical setting (ICU, emergency department, ward) and prediction method (rule-based vs. machine learning).
